entries.title: The Legends - Day 1
entries.body:
I woke up in my old childhood room. As I woke up, I saw my sister shaking me, yelling urgently, “PETER! Wake up! Something weird is in the living room.”

I asked, “What do you mean, ‘something weird’?”

She looked at me with a serious face, saying, “Follow me,” and led me to the living room.

To my surprise, I saw something that looked like a person covered in black goo, with no eyes or mouth. Black goo. External evil!

“All right, Lily, go as quickly as you can to Mom and Dad’s room and don’t stop,” I instructed.

“Okay,” Lily responded purposefully.

When Lily left the room, it stared at me, trying to intimidate me with a blank look.

entries.title: Day 1
entries.body:
I woke up in my old childhood room. As I woke up, I saw my sister shaking me, yelling urgently, “PETER! Wake up! Something weird is in the living room.”

I asked, “What do you mean, ‘something weird’?”

She looked at me with a serious face, saying, “Follow me,” and led me to the living room.

To my surprise, I saw something that looked like a person covered in black goo, with no eyes or mouth. Black goo. External evil!

“All right, Lily, go as quickly as you can to Mom and Dad’s room and don’t stop,” I instructed.

“Okay,” Lily responded purposefully.

When Lily left the room, it stared at me, trying to intimidate me with a blank look.

entries.title: Day 2
entries.body:
From the rude awakening of this guy who was in my house uninvited, I kept staring and waited for what he would do next after my sister went away. It did also...

I knew the Black Goo was planning to kill me in the darkness. Oh, did I say kill? I meant consuming me. It ran toward me and pushed me to the ground to get the chance to do what it hoped, but instantly I moved my body away from it. It turned its head to face mine, snapping its neck, and then formed a face with no nose or eyebrows. It had sharp red teeth and eyes that both stretched to the sides of its face. It leaped to the ground, holding my neck with one arm, and with the other it held its body above mine. Then, with a mischievous smile, it started squeezing my neck slowly.

This is war!

I pushed on one of its arms, causing it to break and for its organism to fall on me with a screech of pain. The Black Goo just stopped. With its arm still on my neck, it sent some of itself onto me.

That means it's a...

entries.title: Day 3
entries.body:
That means it's a protist controlling a host. It felt slimy yet hard when climbing onto my chest, looking like a liquid shadow. It moved like, no, not moved; it glided on the ground like sloosh but still had volume. It pulled itself onto my shoulder with small things like arms, but they were more like grappling strings with a sticky and shiny texture. Not one, but millions were pulling in the direction it wanted to go.

It stretched itself to touch both sides of my body, extending to make ropes with the same texture as itself. Eventually, it had four ropes attached to the ground around me, pulling me against the ground. Nearly in the ground, I reached for the other arm of the organism and broke it. I didn’t stop there; I pulled off the arm.

Then another arm appeared. It was shaped like a samurai sword. Of course, it didn't stop there! It tried to stab me, and then I saw a bunch of light appear to come from my body. It evaporated The Black Goo and left a human with blonde hair and blue eyes.

entries.title: Day 4
entries.body:
The human looked like he hadn't eaten in years. The human looked like a man, but it was hard to tell. I knew from earlier that this person was lost, but not this lost. I didn't know.

I couldn't do anything for him because of the condition he was in, but I could do one thing: tell someone.

So I went to my parents and told them what had happened. They looked at each other with dread, as if they knew this was going to happen. They then responded, "Alright, we know this is confusing, but there is no time to explain anything. Grab Jake and take both him and Lily out of this area. When you get to your school, you'll know what to do."

So Jake, Lily, and I set out on the journey ahead.

entries.title: Day 5
entries.body:
My parents said goodbye, and I finished the fight, beginning a journey filled with questions. My mind tells me not to listen, but a force deep within my spirit urges me to keep going and bring this conflict to an end.

We run outside with a mission: to escape, to flee from the chaos and pain. It doesn't feel right. We need to fight! But we can't. We must keep running if we want to survive.

The Black Goo roars behind eating the world from a big bottomless pit that keeps growing and realizing more organisms. While ahead? There’s salvation.

entries.title: Day 6
entries.body:
There were people fighting back, with tight suits made of a flexible alloy with bright-colored lines all over them and gigantic sword-like weapons especially made for destroying the Black Goo. They seemed alien like the Black Goo, but still like humans. They were the height of a moose, but had the same shape and similar looks, only better. 

The Black Goo had the most alien look. It was the same height as the fighters. Its looks were demon-like, but not completely; it still was a humanoid. 

Then I saw every fighter do exactly what had happened when the light appeared in the fight that I had with The Black Goo.

entries.title: Day 7
entries.body:
The Black Goo evaporated, and just like what happened to me, there were humans left behind. They seemed confused at first, but then they all realized what was happening and grabbed weapons from the fighters. They became fighters themselves, starting a battle, The Battle Of Life.

Jake then looked at me with compassion and said, “Why aren’t we fighting?!”

Almost instantly, I responded, “We ca... You know what, Jake? You’re right. Let’s fight.”

Lily yelled, “No! Mom and Dad said to go to your school, not fight!”

I responded to her in a sharp voice, “Shut up.”

We all then picked up weapons and became fighters.

entries.title: Day 8
entries.body:
The weapon didn’t feel like an ordinary earthly sword; it had energy attached to it, like the feeling of The Bust of Light. It wasn’t only that. The strength in my soul and the fire in my veins surged with it. Energy coursed through my hands, and it felt powerful, like I could tear the ground out from beneath this Black Goo. I could seriously destroy this thing.

It had the shape of a sword, but its end held another blade, with a handle in the middle. The blades were like two tall, singular spikes of gray crystal that I had never seen before.

Lily felt it too, because the moment she touched that weapon, she glared at her enemy with an intense stare, a determined grin, and her head tilted forward. She looked like she was about to destroy. Then she lifted her hands, and something appeared: purple, translucent bubbles.

entries.title: Day 9
entries.body:
She spread out her hands and the bubbles released, moving towards the black goo. They lowered to where it was, and Lily allowed them to touch the black goo and pop, causing scarlet red gas to appear, blinding me.

I heard screeching.

Then it disappeared. Mysteriously, all the black goo was gone, and in their place were shriveled bodies. Just like when the burst of light evaporated the black goo. Everyone that I saw stared at Lily, astonished at what she had done. Some even spoke, "How did she do that?" or "This is impossible."

entries.title: Day 10
entries.body:
One man from the crowd, who was wearing a maroon suit jacket with a green shirt and maroon pants and a helmet that had tinted glass and metal the same color as his jacket, walked up to us and pressed the side of his helmet. He then said, "We found them."

Was he talking about us? I thought to myself as I saw something in the tinted glass covering his face that looked like words, but it was hard to tell because the glass seemed to be made where words seemed blurry to the people on the outside.

I then stared at him to see what he meant by the words he spoke. He saw me and said, "What?" "What do you mean by 'we found them'?"

"Well, we were looking for you and your siblings…"

The man pointed at the crowd behind him and continued, "...this is the group I'm referring to when I say 'we,' and look, we found you!"

entries.title: Day 11
entries.body:
“And why exactly were you looking for us?” I asked suspiciously.

“Because if we didn’t find you, The Black Goo would eat you all up and our home would also be eaten too. That wouldn’t be good, won’t it?” — talking to me like I was a baby and with a grim tone. A great combination!

I was starting to get really annoyed with this man. He was condescending and rude, but what he was saying seemed important to him, and to me it was getting interesting and funny. But it also seemed really confusing. Because I guess I was really annoyed and my brain just wanted to make things overdramatic, I yelled, “What?!” out of impulse.

“Oh, your parents might’ve not told you under such short notice…”

The way he was talking also made Jake annoyed, because the way he looked at the guy had a familiar look to it. WAIT NO! “Jake don’-”

Really fast, Jake moved as he slapped him, but the thing that was different was there were lime green streaks of light that moved with his hand, faster than I could realize. The man flew, like literally flew, away the moment before the hand hit his face. Then Jake just said, “Bro just shut up!” annoyed.

entries.title: Day 12
entries.body:
“How!?” I asked, astonished as the man landed back on the ground.

“First of all, you got some strong powers, kid,” the man said, talking to my brother. “Second of all, me and our people have powers to shape the universe, multiverse, dimensions, and so on, including your parents.”

“So all humans have superpowers?” asked Lily.

“We are not humans.”

“So why are we here?” asked Jake.

“That I will explain later, but we gotta get goin’.”

“Where?”

“To your middle school.”

We started walking again with the man and the crowd with us.

entries.title: Day 13
entries.body:
As we were walking, we all saw another group of fighters. They were wearing suits made of a dark green material, covered in lines of glowing lime-green light. The fighters were battling the black goo and winning easily.

Then I saw the most bizarre thing I'd ever seen in my lifetime. Vine-like tentacles came out of their hands while across from them, the black goo held a girl ten feet in the air with black tentacles around her neck. The fighters' tentacles reached toward the girl, trying to save her.

entries.title: Day 14
entries.body:
I turned back to see the man not looking at the scene, saying, “Come on, Peter,” not even sounding concerned. Instead, he walked the other way. Why would he do that? What about the girl’s safety? It concerned me that he didn’t even react.

I stood there looking at the man and my siblings walk further and further together with the crowd. Behind me, I heard the roar of the battle, the clashes of swords, the screeching of the black goo, and the thud of the fighters falling to the floor and dying.

So I decided to stop trying to get to safety and start fighting.

entries.title: Day 15
entries.body:
I continued watching the battle to see the best point to get in there. I focused on a man who was in the battle. He had a sword and seemed to be the main star. The warrior was slicing through black goo after black goo, together with the whole army, smiling. He was tall, just like me and everyone I knew, and he had brown hair, but before I even got a good look at his face, a black goo ran behind him and stabbed him. The warrior dropped his sword and fell face forward, giving me a chance to fight.

I walked over to him, exposing myself. I grabbed the sword and said, “Thank you,” respectfully.

entries.title: Day 16
entries.body:
When I walked over to the wounded warrior, I saw the battle stop. I mean every black goo and warrior stopped, they all focused on me and some warriors said "another one” in shock. Then it started again when I picked up the sword, every warrior back to their places. But someone in the army yelled “everyone surround him”, loud and sharp. Everyone did what he said but just enough where I was protected on all sides but the front. 

The black goo was different from the one I fought earlier. It had arm blades and instead of eyes stretched to the side of their heads, they had vicious eyes the shape of crystals. They were tall and had scorpion-like legs that didn’t have feet but spikes. But somehow it was all goo.
